item.title: Electrode Geometry-Controlled Quantum Transport in Au–Pentane–Au Molecular Junctions: A DFT–NEGF and Machine Learning Study
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Vijay Kumar Lamba, Sankit Kassa, Deepika Deepika
Molecular electronics offers a route toward continued device miniaturization, but reliable control of charge transport at the molecular scale requires a detailed understanding of the metal–molecule interface. In particular, the role of electrode geometry in determining transport behaviour remains less systematically explored than molecular structure and contact chemistry. Here, we investigate the influence of atomic-scale electrode geometry on the structural, electronic, quantum-transport, thermoelectric, and noise properties of Au–pentane–Au molecular junctions using a combined density functional theory–non-equilibrium Green's function (DFT–NEGF) and machine learning framework. item.title: High-throughput Discovery of Magnetic Rare Earth Transition Metal Alloys
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Shuo Tao, Osman Goni Ridwan, Liqin Ke, Qiang Zhu
We present an accelerated materials discovery framework that combines diffusion-based crystal structure generation with hierarchical screening to identify new rare-earth–transition-metal magnets simultaneously achieving high magnetization and thermodynamic stability. Using this workflow, we systematically explored over 3000 binary (R-T) and ternary (R-T-T ′) compositions spanning R ∈ Y, Sm, T ∈ Fe, Co, Ni, and T ′ ∈ Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Cu, Zn, and filtered approximately 240,000 generated crystal structures through machine-learning interatomic potential prescreening and spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) validation. item.title: Checkerboard-type Zhang-Rice states in overdoped cuprate superconductors
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Xiongfang Liu, Kun Han, Yan Peng, Yuanjie Ning, Jing Wu, Zhaoyang Luo 等16位作者
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77985-0 In cuprate superconductors, the overdoped regime has received comparatively limited attention. Here, broadband optical spectroscopy and DQMC calculations reveal an electronic reconstruction in LSCO beyond x > 0.2, consistent with a checkerboard Zhang–Rice configuration hosting coexisting localized and itinerant carriers.

item.title: Laser experiments recreate solar flare physics and reveal consistent magnetic reconnection rates
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Magnetic reconnection is a process that occurs when the magnetic fields of a conductive plasma quickly rearrange and release massive amounts of stored magnetic energy. It is widely thought to be the underlying mechanism behind cosmic events such as solar flares and substorms in Earth's magnetosphere.

item.title: An extremely stable quantum gas offers a new lens on strongly interacting systems
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Molecular gases are a new form of artificial quantum matter. However, when these molecules collide, they are often lost extremely rapidly. Researchers from Radboud University and Columbia University have been able to suppress this collisional loss, paving the way for strongly interacting quantum matter. This new artificial quantum matter allows researchers to study quantum behavior relevant to electrons in real materials. Their results are published in Science.

item.title: Physicists extend the search for quantum black holes at the LHC
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Physicists at UC Santa Barbara have extended the search for evidence of microscopic black holes produced at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). The formation of these tiny, fleeting objects at the LHC represents one way theorists have sought to resolve anomalies in our understanding of the basic structure of spacetime, while the method used to look for them demonstrates a new way of searching for new particles.

item.title: Enhancing V2X Communication Security Using an MTCNN-LSTM-Based Multilevel Trust Evaluation Framework
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Sanjay Kumar Sonker, Bharat Bhushan Sagar, Vibha Kaw Raina, Md Khalid Jamal
In the evolution of V2X infrastructure deployment, vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication necessitates authentication, privacy, and dependability. Securing the V2X networks and charging issues is critical and more challenging due to the extensive infrastructure. This direction enables trust-based transactions between electric vehicles and the smart grid to fulfill energy consumption. This paper reveals the closed-loop V2X security and energy allocation system that integrates real-time multi-attack detection, dynamic trust evaluation, and battery optimization in an intelligent transportation system. item.title: The Darma Valley at the Himalayan Trijunction: Community, Territoriality, and Security Dynamics in the Borderland of India, China and Nepal
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Rishabh Verma
Darma Valley is a high-altitude region in the Dharchula tehsil of Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand, of the Rang or Darmiya Bhotiya community. Although small, the valley is structurally significant in the interface region along the borders of India, China, and Nepal, and it remains relatively understudied. Darma was one of only six passes officially designated for trade and pilgrimage under the Sino-Indian Agreement of 1954 between the Tibet Region of China and India. The centuries-old trans-Himalayan trading economy that sustained the valley became unviable after the Indo-Tibetan border was closed following the war of 1962, and the region was transformed into a heavily militarised border, guarded by the Indo-Tibetan Border Police.
